rv.q: The restrained portrayal of the lovers’ passion is aesthetically brave, but there’s a downside: In his determination to eschew the easy charms of melodrama, Lloyd slightly undercooks the romance, which in turn diminishes our investment in its terrible ramifications.
Though to be fair, intense over-acting may be for the sake of the crowd, for whom Shakespeare remains a dense and daunting endeavor
By the end, Hainsworth and Jimoh have captured the central characters’ essence so effectively that their mutual demise is still shocking and heartfelt.
